steps.t: A remote user on the Cato Client and a site behind a Socket both enter the nearest PoP.
The single-pass engine makes every decision there; segments 1 to 6 are that engine from six angles.
The flow leaves for the internet, a SaaS application or a private app behind an App Connector.
Segment 7 is what the same engine tells you afterwards: telemetry from every flow in one console.

steps.t: Priya at home on the Cato Client and the Bristol Office behind its Socket reach the nearest PoP.
TLS inspection, staged by category, lets the Internet Firewall match on user, category and application.
The verdict is Allow, Prompt or Block, and every match is written to Events with user, rule and action.

Inside the PoP two stacked nd boxes with badge(1)/badge(2): '1 · TLS inspection' s ['staged by category'] and '2 · Internet Firewall' s ['who · where · action']; pill under them 'Allow · Prompt · Block'. RIGHT (three destinations, one per verdict): nd 'Business SaaS' s ['Allow — category rule'] with mark 'ok' and pill g 'Allow'; nd 'Social media' s ['Prompt — user decides'] with mark 'warn' and pill y 'Prompt'; nd 'Gambling' s ['Block — risky category'] with xmark and pill r 'Block'. BOTTOM RIGHT: nd 'Monitor → Events' s ['user · rule · action'] icon console cls 'soft'. FLOWS: fl-tun from both sources into the PoP; fl-flow (green arrow) PoP→Business SaaS; fl-ha (amber) PoP→Social media; fl-down (red, ends at xmark before the node) PoP→Gambling; fl-dim dashed from the PoP to Events labelled 'every verdict'. steps.t: Priya on the Cato Client and the Bristol Office Socket send every flow to the nearest PoP.
The engine inspects each flow once against IPS, anti-malware, the cloud sandbox and DNS security.
Clean traffic continues; malware, exploits and C2 beacons are blocked at the PoP as attributed events.
The same events feed the Threats Dashboard and, when they belong together, one XDR story.

steps.t: Every user and site already sends its traffic through the PoP, so the SaaS inventory builds from traffic.
The engine identifies the cloud application inline, looks up its risk score and checks the tenant.
Activity decides the action: corporate tenant allowed, personal tenant blocked, risky app browse-only.
Inventory, scores and decisions land in the Cloud Apps Dashboard and the same event stream.

steps.t: Marcus uploads a spreadsheet from the Cato Client; the Bristol Office Socket sends the same kind of flow.
Decrypted once under the TLS inspection policy, the engine asks one more question: does the content match?
The Data Control rule blocks the card-number upload to personal storage; the SharePoint upload is allowed.
The incident, with user, file, matched data type and evidence, lands in Events and the dashboard.

steps.t: Priya connects from two laptops; the Client evaluates the Device Posture Profile on each before any tunnel.
The Client Connectivity Policy admits the compliant device; the failing one gets no tunnel, only an event.
WAN Firewall rule 1 allows Finance plus posture to the ERP application behind the London DC Socket.
Everything beneath rule 1 is the implicit block; both the allow and the block are events under her name.

steps.t: Marcus and a contractor both type app.example.intranet on the Cato Client; neither knows an internal address.
The PoP evaluates the Private Access Policy; for Marcus, Cato DNS answers with a synthetic IP.
His session is brokered over the connector’s outbound DTLS tunnel to the app in the acquired data centre.
The contractor matches no rule, so the lookup is denied and the name does not resolve; nothing is reached.

LEFT: nd 'Marcus · Cato Client' s ['Finance group · posture pass'] icon laptop mark ok at (20,150); nd 'Contractor · Cato Client' s ['No matching rule'] icon laptop mark no at (20,340); a mono T label 'app.example.intranet' between them (both type the same name). TOP CENTRE control plane: nd cls 'dash' 'Private Access Policy' s ['group · posture · app'] icon key at (260,30) with a thin fl-dim (np:0) line down into the PoP. CENTRE: popBox (240,120,270,320) 'Cato PoP' sub 'ZTNA broker · Cato DNS'; inside two verdict boxes: 'Rule matched · Allow' s ['DNS returns synthetic IP'] pill g, and 'No rule · Block' s ['Domain does not resolve'] pill r. RIGHT: site 'Internal application' sub 'acquired DC · LAN' containing nd 'App Connector' s ['outbound DTLS · group'] icon appc at (580,170) and nd 'Internal application' s ['app.example.intranet'] icon server at (580,330); a thin fl-net (LAN) line connector→app labelled 'local forward'. Legend kinds: flow (rule matched), down (no rule), dim (control plane).

steps.t: Priya’s Client and the Bristol Office Socket carry telemetry from the device and the last mile.
The PoP and the global private backbone are the same platform, so the middle mile is measured too.
The egress PoP nearest the app measures Microsoft 365 and the private app behind the London DC Socket.
Experience Monitoring scores each segment on its own; the one off-green node is the fault domain.

diagram.brief: 760x560, left-to-right path with four numbered segments. LEFT: nd 'Remote user' s ['Priya · Cato Client'] icon laptop at (20,150) and site 'Bristol Office' with nd 'Socket X1500' icon building at (20,330); badge(1) on the devices. A short stretch labelled 'ISP last mile' (T, f-m) between the sources and the PoP with badge(2) and pill y 'Fair' on that stretch. CENTRE: fpin 'Cato PoP — London' sub 'single-pass engine' at x≈300, ring 'Global Private Backbone' spanning to a second fpin 'Cato PoP — egress' sub 'nearest the app' at x≈520; badge(3) on the ring. RIGHT: cloud 'SaaS app' sub 'Microsoft 365' at (660,170) and site 'London DC' with nd 'Private app' s ['London DC Socket'] icon server at (600,330); badge(4) on the app links. FLOWS: fl-tun sources→London PoP with the segment-2 stretch drawn fl-ha (amber) to mark the degraded last mile; fl-tun London PoP→egress PoP along the ring (segment 3, green); fl-flow egress PoP→M365 and fl-tun egress PoP→London DC (segment 4, green). BOTTOM STRIP (y 450-540): four nd cls 'soft' score cards in a row: '1 Device' s ['CPU · memory · Wi-Fi'] mark ok; '2 Last mile — Fair' s ['tunnel loss · RTT · jitter'] mark warn; '3 Backbone' s ['PoP to PoP'] mark ok; '4 Application' s ['TTFB · TCP · TLS'] mark ok. Tier label above the strip: 'Experience Monitoring scores each segment on its own — the one off-green node is the fault domain'. Only segment 2 is amber; nothing is red or blocked.
